question:
An Italian transportation company needs to transport some empty containers from its 6 warehouses (located in Verona, Perugia, Rome, Pescara, Taranto, and La Spezia) to major national ports (Genoa, Venice, Ancona, Naples, Bari). The inventory of containers in each warehouse is as follows:

|  | Empty Containers |
| :---: | :---: |
| Verona | 10 |
| Perugia | 12 |
| Rome | 20 |
| Pescara | 24 |
| Taranto | 18 |
| La Spezia | 40 |

The demand at the ports is as follows:

|  | Container Demand |
| :---: | :---: |
| Genoa | 20 |
| Venice | 15 |
| Ancona | 25 |
| Naples | 33 |
| Bari | 21 |

The transportation will be done by a fleet of trucks. The transportation cost for each container is directly proportional to the distance traveled by the truck, at a rate of 30 euros per kilometer. Each truck can transport a maximum of 2 containers. The distances are as follows:

|  | Genoa | Venice | Ancona | Naples | Bari |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Verona | $290 \mathrm{~km}$ | $115 \mathrm{~km}$ | $355 \mathrm{~km}$ | $715 \mathrm{~km}$ | $810 \mathrm{~km}$ |
| Perugia | $380 \mathrm{~km}$ | $340 \mathrm{~km}$ | $165 \mathrm{~km}$ | $380 \mathrm{~km}$ | $610 \mathrm{~km}$ |
| Rome | $505 \mathrm{~km}$ | $530 \mathrm{~km}$ | $285 \mathrm{~km}$ | $220 \mathrm{~km}$ | $450 \mathrm{~km}$ |
| Pescara | $655 \mathrm{~km}$ | $450 \mathrm{~km}$ | $155 \mathrm{~km}$ | $240 \mathrm{~km}$ | $315 \mathrm{~km}$ |
| Taranto | $1010 \mathrm{~km}$ | $840 \mathrm{~km}$ | $550 \mathrm{~km}$ | $305 \mathrm{~km}$ | $95 \mathrm{~km}$ |
| La Spezia | $1072 \mathrm{~km}$ | $1097 \mathrm{~km}$ | $747 \mathrm{~km}$ | $372 \mathrm{~km}$ | $333 \mathrm{~km}$ |

Write a mathematical program to find the transportation policy that minimizes cost and solve it using COPTPY.

def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # ----- Sets -------------------------------------------------------------
    model.warehouses = pyo.Set(initialize=d["warehouses"])
    model.ports = pyo.Set(initialize=d["ports"])
    model.routes = pyo.Set(
        dimen=2,
        initialize=[(i, j) for i in d["warehouses"] for j in d["ports"]],
    )

    # ----- Unit cost per container = rate_per_km * distance -----------------
    def unit_cost(i, j):
        return d["rate_per_km"] * d["distance"][(i, j)]

    # ----- Variables --------------------------------------------------------
    # x[i,j] = number of containers shipped from warehouse i to port j
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.routes, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # ----- Objective --------------------------------------------------------
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(unit_cost(i, j) * m.x[i, j] for (i, j) in m.routes)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # ----- Constraints ------------------------------------------------------
    # Supply: cannot ship more than the warehouse inventory
    def supply_rule(m, i):
        return sum(m.x[i, j] for j in m.ports) <= d["supply"][i]

    model.supply_constraint = pyo.Constraint(model.warehouses, rule=supply_rule)

    # Demand: each port must receive at least its demand
    def demand_rule(m, j):
        return sum(m.x[i, j] for i in m.warehouses) >= d["demand"][j]

    model.demand_constraint = pyo.Constraint(model.ports, rule=demand_rule)

    return model
